name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_BIOMOLECULES_STATEMENT3_Q01 - Functional group identification reactions in D-glucose

questiontext.text:
Given below are three statements:

Statement I: Glucose reacts with hydroxylamine to form an oxime.

Statement II: Glucose adds a molecule of hydrogen cyanide to yield a cyanohydrin.

Statement III: Acetylation of glucose with acetic anhydride gives glucose pentaacetate, confirming the presence of five hydroxyl groups.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
D-Glucose is an aldohexose possessing one aldehyde functional group and five hydroxyl groups along an unbranched six-carbon chain. Carbonyl groups undergo addition and condensation reactions with nucleophiles such as hydrogen cyanide and hydroxylamine, whereas hydroxyl groups undergo esterification with acylating agents like acetic anhydride.

Step 2: Evaluation of the First Statement
When D-glucose is treated with hydroxylamine (\(\mathrm{NH_2OH}\)), the aldehyde group at C1 undergoes condensation to form an oxime (\(\mathrm{CH=N-OH-(CHOH)_4-CH_2OH}\)). This reaction confirms the presence of a carbonyl group. Thus, the statement that glucose reacts with hydroxylamine to form an oxime is correct.

Step 3: Evaluation of the Second Statement
When D-glucose reacts with hydrogen cyanide (\(\mathrm{HCN}\)), nucleophilic addition of cyanide ion to the carbonyl group yields the corresponding cyanohydrin (\(\mathrm{CH(OH)(CN)-(CHOH)_4-CH_2OH}\)). This also confirms the presence of a carbonyl group. Thus, the statement that glucose adds hydrogen cyanide to yield a cyanohydrin is correct.

Step 4: Evaluation of the Third Statement
Acetylation of D-glucose with acetic anhydride in the presence of pyridine yields glucose pentaacetate. Because glucose is a stable compound, no two hydroxyl groups are attached to the same carbon atom. Therefore, the formation of pentaacetate confirms that glucose contains five distinct hydroxyl groups. Thus, the statement that acetylation of glucose with acetic anhydride gives glucose pentaacetate, confirming the presence of five hydroxyl groups, is correct.

Step 5: Final Conclusion
All three statements describing the reactions of glucose are scientifically accurate. Therefore, Statements I, II and III are correct.

answer.text: Statements I, II and III are correct
Statements I and II only are correct

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_BIOMOLECULES_STATEMENT3_Q02 - Glycosidic linkage differences in structural polysaccharides

questiontext.text:
Given below are three statements:

Statement I: Amylose is a water-soluble component of starch composed of an unbranched chain of \(\alpha\)-D-(+)-glucose units held by C1–C4 glycosidic linkages.

Statement II: Amylopectin is a water-insoluble component of starch consisting of branched chains with C1–C4 linkages and branching via C1–C6 glycosidic linkages.

Statement III: Cellulose is a branched polysaccharide composed of \(\alpha\)-D-(+)-glucose units linked by C1–C6 glycosidic linkages.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Polysaccharides are polymers of monosaccharides joined by glycosidic bonds. Starch is a storage polysaccharide composed of two fractions: amylose and amylopectin. Cellulose is the main structural component of plant cell walls, composed of linear glucose chains.

Step 2: Evaluation of the First Statement
Amylose constitutes roughly 15–20% of natural starch and is soluble in water. It is a long, unbranched polymer consisting of 200–1000 \(\alpha\)-D-(+)-glucose units connected exclusively by \(\alpha\)-1,4-glycosidic linkages (between C1 of one unit and C4 of the next). Thus, the statement describing amylose as water-soluble and unbranched with C1–C4 linkages is correct.

Step 3: Evaluation of the Second Statement
Amylopectin forms the remaining 80–85% of starch and is insoluble in water. It is a branched-chain polymer where linear segments contain \(\alpha\)-1,4-glycosidic linkages, and branch points are formed by \(\alpha\)-1,6-glycosidic linkages between C1 of the branching unit and C6 of the chain. Thus, the statement describing amylopectin as water-insoluble with C1–C4 linear linkages and C1–C6 branching linkages is correct.

Step 4: Evaluation of the Third Statement
Cellulose is an unbranched, straight-chain polysaccharide composed exclusively of \(\beta\)-D-(+)-glucose units joined by \(\beta\)-1,4-glycosidic linkages. It does not consist of \(\alpha\)-D-(+)-glucose, nor does it contain branching or C1–C6 linkages. Thus, the statement claiming cellulose is a branched polymer of \(\alpha\)-D-(+)-glucose with C1–C6 linkages is incorrect.

Step 5: Final Conclusion
The first two statements are correct, whereas the third statement is incorrect. Therefore, Statements I and II only are correct.

answer.text: Statements I, II and III are correct
Statements I and II only are correct

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_BIOMOLECULES_STATEMENT3_Q03 - Secondary structure and denaturation of proteins

questiontext.text:
Given below are three statements:

Statement I: In an \(\alpha\)-helix, the polypeptide chain is stabilised by hydrogen bonds between the \(-\mathrm{NH}-\) group of each amino acid residue and the \(>\mathrm{C=O}\) group of an adjacent turn.

Statement II: Fibrous proteins such as keratin and myosin are highly soluble in water due to strong interactions with solvent molecules.

Statement III: During denaturation of proteins, secondary and tertiary structures are destroyed while the primary structure remains intact.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Proteins exhibit hierarchical structures: primary (linear sequence of amino acids linked by peptide bonds), secondary (regular folding patterns like \(\alpha\)-helices and \(\beta\)-sheets maintained by hydrogen bonds), tertiary (overall 3D conformation), and quaternary. Denaturation alters higher-order structures without breaking peptide bonds.

Step 2: Evaluation of the First Statement
In the \(\alpha\)-helix structure, the polypeptide chain coils into a right-handed screw held in shape by intramolecular hydrogen bonds formed between the \(-\mathrm{NH}-\) group of each amino acid residue and the \(>\mathrm{C=O}\) group of a peptide bond in the adjacent helical turn. Thus, the statement regarding the stabilisation of the \(\alpha\)-helix by hydrogen bonding is correct.

Step 3: Evaluation of the Second Statement
In fibrous proteins, polypeptide chains run parallel to one another and are held together by intermolecular hydrogen and disulphide bonds, forming tough, thread-like structures that are insoluble in water. Keratin (present in hair, wool, nails) and myosin (present in muscles) are classic examples of insoluble fibrous proteins. Thus, the statement asserting that fibrous proteins such as keratin and myosin are highly soluble in water is incorrect.

Step 4: Evaluation of the Third Statement
When a native protein is exposed to physical changes (such as heat) or chemical changes (such as changes in pH), the non-covalent hydrogen and ionic bonds are disrupted. The globules unfold and helices uncoil, resulting in the loss of secondary and tertiary structural organisation and biological activity. However, covalent peptide bonds remain unaffected, leaving the primary structure intact. Thus, the statement that denaturation destroys secondary and tertiary structures while preserving primary structure is correct.

Step 5: Final Conclusion
The first and third statements are correct, whereas the second statement is incorrect. Therefore, Statements I and III only are correct.

answer.text: Statements I, II and III are correct
Statements I and II only are correct

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_BIOMOLECULES_STATEMENT3_Q04 - Structural composition of nucleic acids and hormones

questiontext.text:
Given below are three statements:

Statement I: Complete hydrolysis of DNA yields \(\beta\)-D-ribose, phosphoric acid, and the nitrogenous base uracil.

Statement II: In the double-stranded helical structure of DNA, adenine pairs specifically with thymine via two hydrogen bonds, and guanine pairs with cytosine via three hydrogen bonds.

Statement III: The hormone thyroxine is an iodinated derivative of the amino acid tyrosine and regulates metabolic rate in the body.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Nucleic acids (DNA and RNA) are polynucleotides consisting of repeating nucleotide units, each composed of a pentose sugar, a heterocyclic base, and a phosphate group. Hormones are biochemical intercellular messengers produced by endocrine glands; thyroxine is an iodinated amino acid derivative synthesized in the thyroid gland.

Step 2: Evaluation of the First Statement
Complete chemical hydrolysis of DNA (deoxyribonucleic acid) produces \(\beta\)-D-2-deoxyribose, phosphoric acid, and four nitrogenous heterocyclic bases: adenine, guanine, cytosine, and thymine. \(\beta\)-D-ribose and uracil are characteristic components of RNA (ribonucleic acid), not DNA. Thus, the statement that DNA hydrolysis yields ribose and uracil is incorrect.

Step 3: Evaluation of the Second Statement
In the Watson-Crick double-helix model of DNA, two antiparallel polynucleotide chains are held together by complementary base pairs through hydrogen bonds. Specifically, adenine (A) pairs with thymine (T) through two hydrogen bonds (\(\mathrm{A = T}\)), and guanine (G) pairs with cytosine (C) through three hydrogen bonds (\(\mathrm{G \equiv C}\)). Thus, the statement describing the complementary hydrogen bonding between adenine-thymine and guanine-cytosine is correct.

Step 4: Evaluation of the Third Statement
Thyroxine (tetraiodothyronine) is secreted by the thyroid gland and is chemically an iodinated derivative of the aromatic amino acid tyrosine. It plays a critical role in controlling the basal metabolic rate, energy expenditure, and normal growth of the body. Thus, the statement describing thyroxine as an iodinated tyrosine derivative regulating metabolic rate is correct.

Step 5: Final Conclusion
The second and third statements are correct, whereas the first statement is incorrect. Therefore, Statements II and III only are correct.

answer.text: Statements I, II and III are correct
Statements I and II only are correct

Statements II and III only are correct
